reviews.title: Game changer
reviews.contents: I honestly would have never thought an app could help me with Nap time but I was totally wrong! This app is a game changer, my husband and I are amazed and relieved at the same time! Our little fella (second baby) goes down to the minute that the app recommends, so long as you log your naps accurately. I can plan my day and I look out for sleepy cues just on time! He no longer gets overtired and hardly ever fights skeep time as it’s just on time for him. It calculates skeep pressure based on age and stage, all around the science of sleep. As an added bonus, there’s a whole heap of sleep education modules for parents to access as well. Have already gifted the discount to three friends with babies!

reviews.title: Helpful but room for improvement for paid subscription
reviews.contents:
I really wanted to love Napper, but there are a couple of things that make the experience frustrating—especially considering the cost of the app. The biggest issue is that I can’t start or end a nap without a data connection. Even free apps allow you to record and save nap times offline. I completely understand that the app can’t recalculate the rest of the day without data, but it should still reliably save nap start/end times and sync them later. Losing entries or being unable to log naps on the go really affects usability.

Another feature I’d love to see is more personalised guidance around nap transitions. For example, a prompt like “Bedtime is being pushed later—your baby may be ready to transition from 3 to 2 naps,” along with a suggested gradual transition plan. That kind of support would make the app feel more proactive and truly worth the price.

Napper has great potential, but a few improvements could make it so much more useful for parents.

reviews.title: SAVED OUR SLEEP
reviews.contents: The first night of using Napper (and we only downloaded it half way through the day) our baby only woke once. His sleep has consistently got better with much less settling at nap times and he is settled and asleep within minutes. We have been using it 7 days now and our baby slept through the night (with a little bum tap at 2am)! I can’t believe I hadn’t found this app sooner. Learns our little one’s routine and plans accordingly with different wake ups and nap times, the app learns and grows with him. THANK YOU THANK YOU THANK YOU!

reviews.title: Helpful for planning the day
reviews.contents: Napper is so on point with knowing when my baby will need a nap that I've been able to plan my days easier based on when bug needs to nap, if I need to go shopping I know how long I have before I need to be back home for the next nap. It's honestly made my life so much easier and the fact that my husband has his own account as well so he can see when Bub needs a nap, means I don't have tell him or remind him cause he has the information ready available on his phone!!!

reviews.title: Helpful
reviews.contents: Found this app super helpful for keeping on top of getting enough sleep. I like that 2 people can both be logged in so that I could check in on naps while  at work. Also love getting a notification half hour before bubs optimal sleep time as we all know how hard it can be once you pass that window and they are over-tired!! After around a month of use we found he would sometimes fall asleep to the minute of the time the app said. Incredibly accurate!

reviews.title: Love it
reviews.contents: This has been super helpful for me and my bub. I’m not someone who follows a strict schedule or anything and want my baby to lead when she’s sleepy and need naps. So this has been amazing !! It slowly picked up when she may be getting tired based on when I said she was sleeping. It took about a week and it was spot on. It’ll let me know when she might be ready for a nap and it’s almost perfect (depending on if she’s going through a leap or something) down to the 10-15mins either side! Definitely recommend!!!

reviews.title: So thankful
reviews.contents:
My little one was horrible at sleeping and creating a good sleep routine was so important. I was after an app that would help predict when she is due for a sleep and that was free. 
The notifications helped me pick up on her tired queues, log how long her naps were and predict when she was due next so I could plan my day around her naps. 
Once her days naps were consistent with the apps guidance, her night time sleep improved. 

I was lost until I found Napper! It was a game changer as a first time mum and figuring out motherhood.

reviews.title: Amazing
reviews.contents: This app has been the biggest help. My biggest struggle was being confident that my baby was tired and ready to nap. The app has been scarily accurate in knowing when Bub will be getting sleepy and ready to go down. This apps gotten my baby napping in her bassinet rather than the carrier which was all she was sleeping in previously. Can’t recommend this app highly enough for anyone who needs to take some of the guesswork (and mental energy) out of your baby’s napping and sleep!

reviews.title: Bad update
reviews.contents: The update you have done has changed the times to go from the middle of the circle to the bottom. This would be okay - if the times were not so small that you could hardly read them. When you have a baby screaming at you and your trying to check the times, it’s really not handy having them so small that you have to stop moving to see the times since your baby fed or slept. Please change it back, or at least make the times larger at the bottom.

reviews.title: Very useful
reviews.contents:
Found it very useful, but it would be great if the app could track naps when the phone is offline, such as on a plane or abroad with no roaming. Additionally, the ability to edit pauses in sleep cycles or add them after a nap is completed would be helpful. An issue I've encountered is still receiving notifications that my child's nap time is overdue, even when the nap is being tracked. These small improvements would significantly enhance the user experience. Nevertheless, I do enjoy using this app. 

Thanks.
